inputs: company/delegation_policy.yaml: seats, grants, budget ladder, autonomy, functional authority
One AuthorityRequest: action, seat, department, risk, amount, implementer, reviewer
An ExceptionContext the caller fills from the job, review and gate it already holds
invariants: Shadow only: every decision and record refuses to claim authority; mode=enforcing is refused at construction.
Reserved actions come from company/permissions.yaml, never restated; a grant naming one is refused at load.
Deployment authority is classified and granted to nobody; an unrecognised kind is CEO-reserved.
A seat never decides a request it raised, implemented or reviewed; none may overrule an independent control.
Escalation stops at the lowest sufficient seat; a dormant, restricted or vacant seat decides nothing.
A subordinate grant may not exceed its escalation target on risk or budget; authority is granted, never taken.
An unknown ceiling escalates; sibling ceilings may not sum past their parent; money escalates via the CFO, not the reporting line.
outputs: An AuthorityDecision (APPROVED, REJECTED or ESCALATE) with the chain it walked; an ExceptionReport naming why the CEO must see this, empty on success.
ManagementMetrics separating CEO decisions from CEO notifications
A DeploymentDecision saying what authority a deployment kind would need
A ShadowReport proving the canonical CEO stop semantics still hold
purpose: Calculates, in shadow, which seat may approve an action, whether separation of duties allows it, where it escalates, which exceptions the CEO must see, and what authority a deployment would need. It authorizes nothing.
risks: Nine of thirteen employees are dormant, so most department paths still collapse onto the COO.
The two new seats have decided nothing real; five replayed jobs are not a burn-in.
A deployment policy is not an activation.
Scenarios are transcribed from reports on other branches, not read from a store.
title: Company executive delegation and separation of duties (shadow)
